name: GitLab commits native route structural closure (CHAOS-3346)
$limitation: This plan directly targets the GitLab commits claim/client guards, project binding, pagination and window boundaries, nullable row fields, persisted occurrence-time fallback, repository identity precedence and hash input, tenant-scoped exact readback, accepted Python budget, route readiness, and worker activation. The real ClickHouse tenant collision remains an integration-tagged mutation proof. The generic live-Python oracles execute the canonical Python project and commit mappers plus production row builders; this plan does not claim live credentialed GitLab traffic, scheduler activation, schema redesign, or provider-instance semantics.

mutations.rationale: a GitLab commit handler must reject a claim owned by another provider before issuing any request or effect
the commits handler must not accept a different GitLab dataset merely because it shares project credentials
GitLab PRIVATE-TOKEN and URL semantics must come only from a GitLab-resolved canonical client
the fetched project must be the exact numeric project claimed by the leased unit
a capped traversal is incomplete and must not emit an effect or advance the watermark
the client-side upper-window check must mirror the Python producer and exclude future commits
the descending commit traversal must stop at Python's lower-window boundary instead of persisting older commits
the Go row must preserve every non-null GitLab message while retaining null as null
recovery readback must distinguish a nullable message from an empty string

mutations.find: WHERE org_id = ? AND repo_id = ? AND hash = ?
mutations.replace: WHERE org_id != ? AND repo_id = ? AND hash = ?
mutations.rationale: recovery must inspect the claim tenant when identical repository and commit keys exist in another organization
the Go request plan must port the accepted Python GitLab commits budget instead of inventing a lower allowance

mutations.find:
case provider == "gitlab" && dataset == "commits":
		descriptor.Destinations = []string{"git_commits"}
		descriptor.RouteReady = true
		descriptor.RouteEnabled = switches.GitlabCommits
mutations.replace:
case provider == "gitlab" && dataset == "commits":
		descriptor.Destinations = []string{"git_commits"}
		descriptor.RouteReady = false
		descriptor.RouteEnabled = switches.GitlabCommits
mutations.rationale: the completed pair must be visible through the canonical descriptor and checked-in matrix, not left as dead handler code
enabling only GitLab commits must construct the provider-unit worker family rather than dispatching to no handler
when path_with_namespace is absent, GitLab's path remains identity-bearing and must win before a display name shared by projects in different groups
the commit foreign key must hash the canonical namespaced project path, not the ambiguous display name
a missing or invalid authored timestamp must reuse the persisted occurrence instant so retry rows and effect digests remain byte-identical
a missing or invalid committed timestamp must reuse the persisted occurrence instant so retry rows and effect digests remain byte-identical
